shots.what: Frame 0: face to face, inches apart, on a demonstration stage; he pulls a shocked face, a glare, a huge grin, and it gives each back a beat later (brows, lids, jaw, lips); the camera travels between the faces; he is amazed; a smile starts and it watches his mouth
Close on its mouth as the smile begins: the silicone clears over the corner motor; the horn turns, the rod pulls, the skin moves, the smile forms; the clearing closes
The stage, side on: he leans in; the two smiles land together; he is delighted
One pull back: the stage, the LED wall and the people watching; it makes a whole-face expression for them; one films it, two turn to each other, one raises both hands
Across the lab: the mirror frame slides past and reveals the reflection
The reflection: four different test expressions, the motors faintly visible
A person’s lips, very close
The robot’s lips (in the mirror) make the same shapes in the same place in the frame
shots.cont: mouth position and size matched; identity changes, no morph

shots.what: Face to face: his cue starts; its smile starts before his is plain
Back out of the reflection to the whole mirror setup

The workshop where it is built: silicone still translucent over the frame; one engineer works in the cheek with a driver, the other checks the motors on a laptop and looks up; the camera tracks along the bench; Columbia tag
Closer: her fingertip presses its cheek and the silicone gives around it; she lets go, the skin clears, and the motors come on group by group as it tries brows, smile and lips
His face, close: as he smiles the cheek clears over the muscle doing it; it shortens and pulls the corner up and out
Match cut from his mouth corner to the robot’s: only the corner motor shows, its horn, rod and corner moving as one
shots.cont: mouth corner in the same place across the cut

shots.what: The workshop, wide: one engineer runs the slider board; each combination pulls a face nobody asked for; the other laughs, then winces
Split view of one moment: the whole face (left) and its side section (right); the linkages push and pull the lips into four distinct expressions
The visitor’s mouth says the narrated “banana” (syllables timed to the take)
His face: together / open / stretch / toward, each marked as named
The test bay: a researcher turns console knobs one at a time; the camera moves to the head on its stand; its skin clears over the lip motors; each turn moves them; the mouth misses the target shape
shots.cont: mouth position and width matched across the cut

shots.what: The test bay: she slides one fader up; a speaker on a cart plays speech; the jaw opens with every loud moment and nothing else
A sock puppet rises beside the robot, flapping in sync
shots.cont: jaw flap continues across the cut

shots.what: The researcher’s deadpan look at the pair
She leans to the desk microphone and says the word slowly; facing her, its lips follow her sound; the camera moves from her to it
The lab with the mirror: it turns to its reflection
The reflection, close: a trial, its motors showing through the skin
A run of trials: each face it makes is captured with the commands that made it
The reflected mouth, very close: these motors, this mouth shape
A new combination; then the camera goes into the reflection’s cheek until the skin fills the frame
The workbench: she pulls a tab on a clamped silicone sheet and the whole area around it stretches; then she lifts a metal bracket and turns it: it moves as one piece
shots.cont: skin fills the frame on both sides of the cut

shots.what: Close on the pulled point: the surface around it moves with it, the lip corner follows
The face on the bench and, on the laptop beside it, the same face as the controller sees it; a smile forms on both at once; the engineer nods
The robotics lab, wide: an arm stacking blocks, a rover crossing the floor, another head practising; ours turns away from its mirror
Its gaze lands in the recording alcove; the monitor comes on
People: two cast members talking, one after the other
Over the robot’s shoulder the camera goes into the screen
The screen’s scene becomes the frame: a person speaking close to the camera
shots.cont: the screen content is the same scene, framed identically

shots.what: Another person in profile on a street, lips moving
Another, talking in a kitchen
Someone singing on a small stage
A dark room lit by a wall of screens: a different person speaking or singing on each, each changing clip on its own beat; it looks from face to face
One person, one sample: the sound runs beneath them; the camera closes on the mouth
A person’s lips, very close, saying that example
The robot’s lips in the same place, making the same shapes
One move along the signal: speaker -> trace -> the learned map lights the matching shape -> cable -> motors -> lips
The robot, its lips moving with that speech
A dark testing room: two identical heads hear the same speech; the left only flaps its jaw with the loudness, late; the right makes the learned shapes on time; wide, then close on each mouth
Profile: sung vowels, held
Front: a recording in an untrained language, lips still following
The studio: it keeps time with a recording in a language nobody there speaks; through the control-room glass the engineer listens, shrugs and smiles
Back at the demonstration: on stage it lip-syncs to a recording from the speaker beside it; the audience watches its mouth
Its mouth, close: looking like speaking
In the audience, one of them listens to the words, head on one side, and frowns
Behind it on the stage, looking out over the audience
Its mouth still speaking, then stopping
B: the person’s lips close fully; the robot’s leave a gap (large split)
W: rounded and pushed forward; the robot under-rounds
The gap, very close, ringed
In the audience, someone leans in and narrows their eyes at its mouth
A hotel reception: he comes up to the counter and leans in to a robotic assistant; it turns to him in two stiff steps; he hesitates and eases back
The robot, waiting
He tells good news, a letter in hand (silent)
The robot stares; slow push
His smile completes; the letter lowers
The robot’s smile switches on, late and fast
Over the assistant’s shoulder: its late smile at the edge of frame; across the counter, his awkward reaction
The test bay set for the timing study: a participant across a small table from the head; the researcher at her console starts the session; 2024 tag
Screen insert: the face
Corners and cheeks marked; the small changes begin
The robot’s eye camera
The predicted smile, dashed, over the mouth
The corner motor carries out the translated movement
Face to face, side on: on him as his smile begins; the camera moves to the robot, whose smile starts while his is still coming; it pulls back as both reach the full smile together
The bay again, wider: both smiling; the researcher smiles and nods
The corner motor, very close, starting the smile
His smile, very close
Its smile in the same place in the frame
shots.cont: mouth position matched; identity changes, no morph

shots.what: Back at the reception counter: this time its smile arrives with his, and he lights up, leaning in
From the smile, one pull back: stand, table, console, camera on its tripod, the control-room window: an experiment
The smile; the camera draws back as the motors under it show through
An imagined concourse where such faces are ordinary: kiosk heads talking with passers-by
Possible future: at home on a video call; he talks to the laptop; on its screen the assistant lifts its eyes to him
The call full screen: the assistant answers, its lips following its own voice; his self-view in the corner
The gallery view: him and the assistant side by side; he smiles and its smile arrives with his
A tutor: a hand turns the workbook page; the head watches across the table
An assistant at a help desk: it turns to him, smiles, looks toward the door
He leans in to read a humanoid assistant’s face
Its well-timed smile; one push in to the opening’s framing
The finale on the stage, from the audience: the two face to face in the spotlight; his smile begins; the camera moves in
Side on, close: its smile arrives with his; he leans in, delighted
The face-off from the first frame, both smiling now; as the last words land the robot’s eyes leave him and come to us
